MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 10, 2025
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ruesch at
5:00 p.m., on June 10, 2025, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on June 5, 2025, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at the
Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Ruesch

Absent:  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Staff Present:  Elaine Lister, City Manager
  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley, City Attorney
  Ellis Chang, Director of Administrative Services
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel – Existing Litigation Paragraph (1) of subdivision (d) of
  Section 54956.9 Janice Kronik Gath, et. al v. Mission Viejo OCSC Case No. 30-2024-
  01376969-CU-MC-CJC

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:00pm Mayor Ruesch recessed to Closed Session. At the hour of 6:01pm Mayor
Ruesch reconvened the meeting with all five Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley announced that there was no reportable action for CS1.
City Council Minutes  1  June 10, 2025
 INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Ruesch

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize Caden Bunge and Hudson Moline for Their Act of Heroism

  Mayor Ruesch present Certificates of Heroism to Caden Bunge and Hudson Moline.

Mayor Ruesch provided an update on some of his goals. He mentioned the new addition of the
“Get Involved!” portal on the city’s website which focuses on community engagement. The posting
portal for “Comments on Staggering of Districts”, which has received a lot of comments, however,
Mayor Ruesch did apologize for the previous Friday as there was a technical issue, which has since
been resolved, and all comments have been posted to date. He also mentioned the link to the police
blotter. Lastly, Mayor Ruesch announced the launch of a photo contest asking residents to share
their images of Mission Viejo on the City’s website. The Council shall select a few photos to be
featured during the August 26 City Council meeting that shall be posted on the City’s website and
social media platforms. In addition, he shall select a personal favorite, and the photographer will
receive a City of Mission Viejo gift bag of items.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Robert Breton, M.V.: Spoke on how the city prides itself on being fiscally responsible, on budget
priorities, and the recruitment and retention of staff. He praised staff, stated that the employees are
the city’s greatest asset and asked for a slight change in the City’s priorities.

Dolores Thompson, M.V.: Spoke on the Character program/traits, and its relevance to the peaceful
weekly Wednesday demonstrations. She referred to the recent Facebook post of vandalism on the
public sidewalk and questioned why the FBI was notified?

Mary Carlson, M.V.: Commented on the invocation and its constant reference to God. Stated there
are other religions and gave her own Invocation. She also expressed her concern of first amendment
rights during the weekly rallies on La Paz and Marguerite, and the implication they are responsible
for the sidewalk vandalism.

Paola Trumbly, M.V.: Listed various events she has supported/organized in the city. Extended an
invitation to the City Council to attend the Second Annual Mission Viejo Pride Event on June 21,
at Saddleback College.

Laura Lacko, M.V.: Stated she witnessed the spraying of the sidewalk. Read a statement from
Tristan Kern de Gonzalez, on the injustice of his husbands passing in San Antonio Texas, and
thanked the Council for supporting the Pride Event.

City Council Minutes  2  June 10, 2025
 Carolyn Gatto, M.V.: Shared she is pleased Captain Ivins has made an appearance, during the
Wednesdays protests over the past few weeks. Referred to the various social media posts pertaining
to the vandalism on the city sidewalk in the vicinity of where the weekly protests take place, thus
creating a potential situation for disruption and putting participants in danger.

Laycee Barragato, M.V.: Invited all Council Members to attend the Pride Event on June 21, at
Saddleback College. Commended the Council on recognizing the Jewish Community and anti-
sematic hatred; however, she stated there are other marginalized communities that require the
Council’s attention. Lastly, she thanked Council Member Vasquez for standing up for all citizens
of Mission Viejo.

Michael Rotcher, M.V.: Spoke of his experience attending the peaceful non-confrontational rallies
at the corner of La Paz and Marguerite. Voiced his concern on the graffiti incident and how all the
social media may compromise the safety of protesters. Suggested, a carefully worded retraction is
appropriate and supports the city’s efforts in protecting everyone’s safety.

Hayley Stangland-Spain, M.V.: Shared her experience at last year’s pride event and invited all
Council Members to the upcoming Pride Event. Stated, she is grateful to Council Member Vasquez
for standing up for our community.

Tom Moore, M.V.: Stated he lives in the vicinity of City Hall and regularly walks to Council and
Commission meetings. Referred to the corner sign on La Paz & Marguerite and its display of city
events, and Character Word of the Month.

Allyson Lorrimer, M.V.: Voiced her concerns on the danger of E-bikes.

Melissa Fieber, M.V.: Spoke of previous requests to make Mission Viejo a Sanctuary City.
Questioned the Council on ensuring Mission Viejo residents’ rights being violated, spoke of ICE
(Immigration and Customs Enforcement), DEI (Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion) initiatives, and
voiced her concerns of protecting everyone, visitors and tourists alike.

Carlos Pianelli, M.V.: Mentioned the riots in Los Angles, the LAPD, National Guards, Marines,
January 6, 2021, his conversation with Congresswoman Young Kim and concluded by stating, we
as a people need to stand together.

Stacy Holmes, M.V.: Spoke of class warfare and the impact it will have on generations to come.
He also mentioned Congresswoman Young Kim’s recent vote in the House. Lastly, he spoke on the
budget, stated that he agrees with Mr. Breton’s comments on not losing staff, and to look within the
budget to take care of Mission Viejo residents.

Lynn Holmes, M.V.: Stated she supports the pride event and shall be attending. She reminded
Council Members to support their constituents and encouraged them to attend the Pride Event. She
added, as leaders Council Members need to be seen at all events and demonstrate Character Word
traits.

City Council Minutes  3  June 10, 2025
 Lynne Haynes, M.V.: Spoke as a regular attendee of the protests at the corner of La Paz &
Marguerite. Referenced the vandalism in question and its implication of being tied to protesters.
Finally, she added, exercising her constitutional rights should be respected and not vilified.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ruesch, to approve the Consent
Calendar outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Bucknum

 1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of May 27, 2025, as presented.

 2.  General Check Register Dated May 16, 2025, in the Amount of $1,241,527.24

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 3.  General Check Register Dated May 23, 2025, in the Amount of $849,527.40

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 4.  Golf Check Register Dated May 16, 2025, in the Amount of $29,513.07

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 5.  Golf Check Register Dated May 23, 2025, in the Amount of $93,664.37

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April 2025

  Received and filed.

 7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for April 2025

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  4  June 10, 2025
  8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for April 2025

  Received and filed.

 9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April 2025

  Received and filed.

 10.  Investment Management Services

  Approved the Agreement with Chandler Asset Management, Inc. (A25-19) for investment
  management services for a three-year period July 1,2025,5 through June 30, 2028, with the
  option to renew in two-year increments thereafter.

 11.  Establish an Appropriations Limit for the 2025-26 Fiscal Year

  Adopted Resolution 25-20 Establishing an Appropriations Limit for the 2025-26 Fiscal Year.

 12.  Council Policy 0300-8 Management and Budget Policies

  Adopted Resolution 25-21 Adopting Revised Council Policy for Management and Budget
  Policies (0300-8).

 13.  Fire Hazard Severity Zones (FHSZ) Maps

  Adopted Ordinance 25-355 Adopting and Designating the State Fire Marshals 2025
  Recommended Local Responsibility Area Fire Hazard Severity Zones (Fhsz) Maps, Without
  Revisions, Pursuant To California State Law.

 14.  Professional Services for Planning Services to Develop Objective Design Standards for
  New Residential Development

  Approved the Third Amendment with JBZ, INC. DBA JZMK Partners for Planning
  Consulting Services for the Development of Objective Design Standards for New Residential
  Development to $163,000.

 15.  Revisions to City of Mission Viejo Personnel Policies

  Adopted Resolution 25-22 Providing for the Revisions to Select Personnel Policies.

 16.  Senior Mobility Program

  (1) Approved the City’s Senior Mobility Program Third Amendment to increase contract
  amount by $350,000; and (2) approved the Fourth Amendment which changes the
  contractor’s DBA from California Yellow Cab to OCY Management, LLC.

City Council Minutes  5  June 10, 2025
  17.  Professional Services  for  Community  Development  Block  Grant  Program
  Administration

  Approved Agreement for Community Development Block Grant Administration Services
  (A25-20) from July 1, 2025, to June 30, 2027, in an amount not to exceed $85,000, pending
  City Council approval of the 2025-2027 budget.

 18.  Professional Services for Housing Rehabilitation Program Consultation and
  Implementation

  Approved Agreement for Housing Rehabilitation Program Consultation and Implementation
  Services (A25-21) from July 1, 2025, to June 30, 2027, in an amount not to exceed $60,000
  ($30,000 /year), pending City Council approval of the 2025-2027 budget.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

19. Amendment to Specific Fees for Animal Services, Library, Planning and Recreation
  Programs and Oso Creek Golf Course

  Director of Administrative Services Ellis Chang presented the staff report.

  Mayor Ruesch opened and closed the Public Hearing at 7:13 pm

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ruesch, to (1) Conduct a
  Public Hearing on the Proposed Animal Services, Library, Planning, Recreation and Oso
  Creek Golf Course User Fees; and (2) adopt Resolution 25-23 Amending Specific Fees for
  Animal Services, Library, Planning, and Recreation Programs and Oso Creek Golf Course.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

NEW BUSINESS

 20. Review of 2025-2027 Proposed Budget

  Director of Administrative Services Ellis Chang and Human Resources Manager Monique
  Goetz presented the staff report.

  Robert Breton, M.V.: Spoke of lower salaries/benefits, cost of living, and losing employees to
  other cities. He stated employee turnover has quadrupled in the last budget cycle and suggested
  adjusting salary and merit increases. He concluded by stating the city needs to be more
  competitive in the job market in order to continue to attract and retain quality employees.

City Council Minutes  6  June 10, 2025
   Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Asked Council to protect the library budget and allocate some funding
  from the general fund to the library. She referred to Congresswoman Young Kim’s approval
  of House Bill 1 and its impact on the library’s grant funding. Lastly, she mentioned the city is
  losing experienced staff to other cities.

  Liz Spencer, M.V.: Spoke of bringing solutions to Mission Viejo to stimulate economic
  growth. She introduced Ms. Oliver, CEO of Little Big Farms, and together they offered their
  services/programs to increase the City’s revenue.

  Michelle O’Brien, M.V.: In addition to Mr. Breton’s comments pertaining to employees,
  Michelle stated that potential applicants also look at salaries, benefits and staff turnover, and
  that is something the city should take into consideration. In closing, she added that she
  supports the proposed 2025-27 budget and thanked the Council.

  Council Members asked various questions and made comments.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to (1)
  Review and discuss the 2025-27 proposed budget; (2) direct staff to place the 2025-27
  proposed budget on the June 24, 2025, City Council agenda for adoption; (3) adopt
  Resolution 25-24 Amending the City's Salary Schedule to be effective July 1, 2025, and
  Authorized Position Schedule effective July 5, 2025; and (4) earmark $3,500 for the Marine
  & Sailors Adoption Committee welcome packages.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

21. Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Received written report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

22.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

City Council Minutes  7  June 10, 2025
 Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell reported that Costco just closed escrow in Foothill Ranch on the Regal
Cinemas location and shall be building a new Costco Warehouse in its place. He mentioned the
small brush fire near the Aquatic Center this past Friday, and thanked OCFA for putting it out so
quickly. Lastly, he shared that the first ONOC (Oceana National Olympic Committee) training
camp is underway, and a team from Finland visited the city last week with an interest of training in
Mission Viejo as well as the current Netherlands team.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley highlighted some of the events she recently attended; the Groundbreaking
Ceremony for the new stadium project at Capistrano Valley High School, OCFA’s Best & Bravest
Ceremony, Animal Services Volunteer Appreciation Luau, City of Hope Orange County Ceremony
& Survivorship Celebration, and the Santa Margarita Water District Water Festival.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez also attended the Groundbreaking Ceremony for the new stadium project
at Capistrano Valley High School. She shared that last week her eldest daughter graduated from
Capistrano Valley High School, and she attended the ceremony at Saddleback College, at which
she also saw Captain Ivins. She had unique honor of sitting on stage with other elected officials
with graduating seniors, which was wonderful, and she expressed how happy she is for her
daughter. She concluded by stating she has family vising and has had a great week spending time
with family.

Mayor Ruesch

Mayor Ruesch mentioned he had the opportunity to ride the MV Shuttle with former Mayor Dave
Leckness. He shared that on Friday evening he and Council Member Goodell attended a concert at
Segerstrom Concert Hall. It was the final performance of Carl St.Clair of the Pacific Symphony,
and also Commissioner Robert Breton’s final singing performance. Also, on Sunday Mayor Ruesch
went to see Life of Pi at Segerstrom, a truly spectacular performance. Lastly, he closed with the
following quote ~ “if you’re the smartest person in the room, maybe you’re in the wrong room”.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:45p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ruesch adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, June 24, 2025, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of June 24, 2025
City Council Minutes  8  June 10, 2025
